message.what: G1-G2 geomagnetic activity and elevated solar particle levels may continue as the significant space weather event subsides.
message.where: Worldwide and Earth's orbit. Higher-latitude regions above 55 degrees remain the primary area of concern.
message.when: There is a 60% chance that G1-G2 conditions will continue from 1800 UTC Mon May 13 2024 through 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024. Earliest End: 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024 Latest End: 1200 UTC Tue May 14 2024
message.duration: Minimum Remaining Duration: 6 hours Maximum Remaining Duration: 18 hours
message.confidence: There is a 30% chance that G1-G2 conditions will continue beyond 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024 through 1200 UTC Tue May 14 2024. Confidence is high that G5 activity has ended.
message.impacts: Power systems may continue to experience weak fluctuations, especially at higher latitudes. HF communication and GNSS performance may remain degraded at higher latitudes. Low-Earth-orbit satellites may continue to experience increased drag. Elevated particle levels may remain a concern for aviation, satellite, and other radiation-sensitive operations.
message.additional_details: This Statement supplements the active Space Weather Warning; it does not end the Warning. The Warning remains in effect through 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024 while SWPC confirms that conditions remain below G3. Partners may begin planning a transition from heightened operations to normal monitoring as sector-specific procedures allow.
message.next_update: No later than 0000 UTC Tue May 14 2024, or sooner if conditions change.
